diagnostics.message: :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_launch_template.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

aws_autoscaling_group.ng has an explicit depends_on on aws_launch_template.ng, but it already references aws_launch_template.ng[each.key].id (and .latest_version) inside its mixed_instances_policy, so the ordering is established implicitly. The explicit depends_on entry is redundant.

aws_eks_node_group.ng has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.ng, but it already references aws_iam_role.ng.0.arn via node_role_arn, so the ordering is established implicitly. The explicit depends_on entry is redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.ng depends_on the node role's policy attachments eks-ng, eks-cni and ecr-read, but omits aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write, which is also attached to aws_iam_role.ng (when app-mesh/X-Ray is enabled). The X-Ray daemon runs on these nodes and needs AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess on the node role before it starts, so this attachment should be ordered before the node group completes, exactly like the other node-role policies.

aws_eks_node_group.ng depends_on the node role's policy attachments eks-ng, eks-cni and ecr-read, but omits aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write, which is also attached to aws_iam_role.ng (when app-mesh/X-Ray is enabled). The workload X-Ray daemon relies on AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess on the node role, so this attachment should be ordered before the node group completes, consistent with the other node-role policy attachments.
